rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source warns that people will overstep in supplication and says it is enough to ask for Paradise and its means and seek refuge from Hell and its means.
rows.anchor: سيكون قوم يعتدون في الدعاء ، وحسب المرء أن يقول : اللهم إني أسألك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the prohibition on corruption after reform with God's promise to forgive whoever repents and acts rightly.
rows.anchor: ولا تفسدوا فى الارض بعد إصلاحها } كقوله : { وإنى لغفار لمن تاب وامن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine noun raḥma takes the masculine adjective qarīb by interpreting mercy as kinship or showing mercy.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر { قريب } على تأويل الرحمة بالرحم أو الترحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīb may modify an omitted masculine noun, meaning a thing that is near.
rows.anchor: أو لأنه صفة موصوف محذوف ، أي شيء قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīb may follow faʿīl used with passive meaning, as in qatlā and asrā.
rows.anchor: أو على تشبيهه بفعيل الذي هو بمعنى مفعول كما شبه ذاك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīb may have the form of a verbal noun, like naqīḍ and ḍaghīb.
rows.anchor: أو على أنه بزنة المصدر ، الذي هو النقيض والضغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīb may be masculine because the femininity of raḥma is nonliteral.
rows.anchor: أو لأن تأنيث الرحمة غير حقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading nushuran is a verbal noun of nashara; its accusative is either cognate with sending/spreading or circumstantial, meaning spread out.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( نشرا وهو مصدر نشر . وانتصابه إما لأن أرسل ونشر متقاربان ، فكأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nushuran is also read as the plural of nushūr.
rows.anchor: ونشرا جمع نشور . ونشرا تخفيف نشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nashran is a lightened form of nashr, like rusul and rusl.
rows.anchor: ونشرا تخفيف نشر ، كرسل ورسل

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masrūq reads nushuran to mean things spread out, with faʿl used in a passive sense.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مسروق : ( نشرا ) ، بمعنى منشورات ، فعل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bushran is the plural of bashīr.
rows.anchor: وبشرا جمع بشير . وبشرا بتخفيفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading lightens bushran.
rows.anchor: وبشرا جمع بشير . وبشرا بتخفيفه . وبشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bushran with fatḥa is a verbal noun from bashshara, meaning bearers of glad tidings.
rows.anchor: وبشرا بفتح الباء مصدر من بشره بمعنى بشره ، أي باشرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds come before God's mercy, meaning the rain, among the greatest blessings and most beneficial effects.
rows.anchor: بين يدى رحمته } أمام رحمته ، وهي الغيث الذي هو من أتم النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqallat means that the wind-borne clouds carried and lifted their load; the word derives from the lifter's sense that the load is small.
rows.anchor: أقلت } حملت ورفعت ، واشتقاق الإقلال من القلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavy clouds are cloud masses heavy with water.
rows.anchor: سحابا ثقالا } سحائب ثقالا بالماء جمع سحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in saqnāhu refers grammatically to the masculine word for cloud; taking the clouds by their meaning would call for feminine agreement.
rows.anchor: سقناه } الضمير للسحاب على اللفظ ، ولو حمل على المعنى كالثقال لأنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dead land is a place without life or one needing irrigation; the phrase means for its watering.
rows.anchor: لبلد ميت } لأجل بلد ليس فيه حيا ولسقيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in fa-anzalnā bihi can refer to the land, the cloud, or the driving of the cloud.
rows.anchor: فأنزلنا به } بالبلد أو بالسحاب أو بالسوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following phrase about bringing out fruit has the same referential possibilities and describes that same bringing forth.
rows.anchor: وكذلك { فأخرجنا به . . . } مثل ذلك الإخراج وهو إخراج الثمرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two acts of bringing things forth are alike: each restores something after its creation, so reflection should show no difference between them.
rows.anchor: نخرج الموتى لعلكم تذكرون } فيؤديكم التذكر إلى أنه لا فرق بين الإخراجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good land is fertile and has generous soil; the bad land is saline or barren and grows nothing useful.
rows.anchor: والبلد الطيب } الأرض العذاة الكريمة التربة { والذى خبث } الأرض السبخة التي لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By its Lord's leave means by God's enabling; it is circumstantial and contrasts with poor, worthless growth.
rows.anchor: بإذن ربه } بتيسيره وهو في موضع الحال ، كأنه قيل : يخرج نباته حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading the land itself grows its plant; another analysis omits the genitive head 'plant' and promotes its dependent pronoun to subject, or supplies 'the plant of the bad land'.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يخرج نباته ) أن يخرجه البلد وينبته وقوله : { والذى خبث } ، فحذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakdan is read with an open kāf as a verbal noun meaning poor growth, or with a silent kāf for ease, as in the expression nazaha ʿan al-rayb.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( نكدا ) بفتح الكاف على المصدر . أي ذا نكد . ونكدا ، بإسكانها للتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable contrasts people whom exhortation and warning benefit with those whom nothing affects.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل لمن ينجع فيه الوعظ والتنبيه من المكلفين ، ولمن لا يؤثر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the fertile and barren land as Adam and his descendants, among whom are good and wicked people.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : آدم وذريته منهم خبيث وطيب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda compares a believer who hears, understands, and benefits from scripture to fertile land that grows after rain; the unbeliever is the opposite.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : المؤمن سمع كتاب الله فوعاه بعقله وانتفع به ، كالأرض الطيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The illustration digresses from the sequence after the mention of rain on dead land and the fruit brought out by it.
rows.anchor: وهذا التمثيل واقع على أثر ذكر المطر ، وإنزاله بالبلد الميت ، وإخراج الثمرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same kind of variation is how God turns the signs over and repeats them for grateful believers to reflect and learn.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك التصريف { نصرف الايات } نرددها ونكررها { لقوم يشكرون } نعمة الله وهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with yāʾ makes the phrase mean that God turns the signs.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يصرف ) بالياء أي يصرفها الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-yadharaka may coordinate with yufsidu: leaving Moses unrestrained would enable the corruption Pharaoh alleged and abandoning Pharaoh and his gods.
rows.anchor: ويذرك } عطف على { * يفسدوا } لأنه إذا تركهم ولم يمنعهم ، وكان ذلك مؤديا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, wa-yadharaka answers the question with wāw like fāʾ; al-Ḥuṭayʾa's verse supplies the pattern.
rows.anchor: أو هو جواب للاستفهام بالواو كما يجاب بالفاء ، نحو قول الحطيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative can be explained by an implicit an, asking whether Pharaoh would let Moses go and thereby leave Pharaoh and his gods.
rows.anchor: والنصب بإضمار ( أن ) تقديره : أيكون منك ترك موسى ، ويكون تركه إياك وآلهتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading coordinates with 'Do you leave Moses?' and asks whether he will leave Pharaoh and his gods; it may instead be independent or circumstantial.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ويذرك وآلهتك بالرفع عطفا على أتذر موسى ، بمعنى : أتذره وأيذرك ، يعني

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the verb in the jussive, treating it like yufsidu and comparing the reading fa-aṣṣaddaq wa-akun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( ويذرك بالجزم ) ، كأنه قيل : يفسدوا ، كما قرىء : { فأصدق وأكن من

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reads wa-nadharaka with nūn and the accusative: Pharaoh's people would be diverted from his worship and abandon it.
rows.anchor: ونذرك ) ، بالنون والنصب ، أي يصرفنا عن عبادتك فنذرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant wa-ilāhatika means 'your worship'.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ويذرك وإلاهتك ) ، أي عبادتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Pharaoh's people called the believers' mass conversion after the magicians' faith corruption and feared losing power.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنهم قالوا له ذلك ، لأنه وافق السحرة على الإيمان ستمائة ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says Pharaoh made idols for his people to worship as intermediaries bringing them near him, like idolaters' claim that idols bring them near God.
rows.anchor: وقيل : صنع فرعون لقومه أصناما وأمرهم أن يعبدوها تقربا إليه كما يعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This intermediary explanation is connected to the claim that idols bring worshippers near God, while Pharaoh calls himself the highest lord.
rows.anchor: ويقولون : ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى ، ولذلك قال : أنا ربكم الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens to resume killing the boys, reasserting dominance and showing that Moses' success did not weaken his rule.
rows.anchor: من قتل الأبناء ، ليعلموا أنا على ما كنا عليه من الغلبة والقهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed killing would also prevent the populace from thinking Moses was the foretold child destined to end Pharaoh's rule and from following him.
rows.anchor: ولئلا يتوهم العامة أنه هو المولود الذي أخبر المنجمون والكهنة بذهاب ملكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses tells the Israelites this after Pharaoh threatens their sons, to calm and comfort them and promise victory.
rows.anchor: قال لهم ذلك حين قال فرعون : سنقتل أبناءهم فجزعوا منه وتضجروا يسكنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reminds them of God's promise to destroy the Copts and give Israel their land and homes.
rows.anchor: ويذكر لهم ما وعد الله بني إسرائيل من إهلاك القبط وتوريثهم أرضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is a new independent statement, whereas the prior 'the chiefs said' is connected to the preceding clause.
rows.anchor: هي جملة مبتدأة مستأنفة . وأما { وقال الملا } ( الأعراف : 127 ) فمعطوفة على ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite 'earth' may mean Egypt specifically, as in the linked verse about inheriting the earth, or earth generically, including Egypt as a member of the class.
rows.anchor: إن الارض لله } يجوز أن تكون اللام للعهد ويراد أرض مصر خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic reading is illustrated by Ḍamra's line about a human being's two small organs: it means humanity in general while primarily applying to an individual.
rows.anchor: كما قال ضمرة : إنما المرء بأصغريه ، فأراد بالمرء الجنس ، وغرضه أن يتناوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good end promises a favorable outcome to the God-fearing among both Israelites and Copts, and that God's will encompasses them.
rows.anchor: والعاقبة للمتقين } بشارة بأن الخاتمة المحمودة للمتقين منهم ومن القبط ، وأن المشيئة

rows.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd read al-ʿāqibata in the accusative, coordinated with al-arḍ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ : ( والعاقبة للمتقين ) بالنصب : أبي وابن مسعود ، عطفا على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites refer to the killing of their sons before Moses' birth and its resumption after he was commissioned, as well as enslavement, forced labor, and punishment.
rows.anchor: يعنون قتل أبنائهم قبل مولد موسى عليه السلام إلى أن استنبئى ، وإعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' statement that God may destroy their enemy openly clarifies the earlier implicit promise of Pharaoh's destruction and Israel's succession in Egypt.
rows.anchor: تصريح بما رمز إليه من البشارة قبل . وكشف عنه ، وهو إهلاك فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will see their good and bad deeds, gratitude and ingratitude, and reward them accordingly.
rows.anchor: فيرى الكائن منكم من العمل حسنه وقبيحه وشكر لنعمة وكفرانها ، ليجازيكم على

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: A report tells of ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd reciting this verse when al-Manṣūr could not provide another loaf, then reminding him after he became caliph that his conduct remained to be seen.
rows.anchor: وعن عمرو بن عبيد رحمه الله أنه دخل على المنصور قبل الخلافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asaf means intense anger, as in the linked verse about God's anger and punishment; another view takes it to mean grief.
rows.anchor: الأسف : الشديد الغضب { فلما ءاسفونا انتقمنا منهم } ( الزخرف : 55 ) وقيل : هو الحزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalafتموني means you took my place as my successors after me.
rows.anchor: خلفتمونى } قمتم مقامي وكنتم خلفائي من بعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may target the calf-worshipping Samaritan and his followers, or Israel's leaders, including Aaron and the believers among them; the latter is supported by Moses' earlier charge.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخطاب إما أن يكون لعبدة العجل من السامري وأشياعه أو لوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blame is for replacing God's worship with the calf, or for failing to restrain those who worshipped something other than God.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : بئس ما خلفتموني حيث عبدتم العجل مكان عبادة الله ، أو حيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the grammar of biʾs, the subject is implicit and explained by mā khalafتمūnī; the omitted object of blame is their bad succession.
rows.anchor: الفاعل مضمر يفسره ما خلفتموني . والمخصوص بالذم محذوف تقديره : بئس خلافة خلفتمونيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'After me' means after witnessing Moses affirm God's oneness, reject partners, and purify worship.
rows.anchor: معناه من بعد ما رأيتم مني ، من توحيد الله ، ونفي الشركاء عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means after Moses had kept Israel committed to monotheism and restrained their desire for a calf, recalled by their earlier request for a god.
rows.anchor: أو من بعد ما كنت أحمل بني إسرائيل على التوحيد . وأكفهم عما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A successor should follow the predecessor's way rather than contradict it; the linked verse likewise speaks of later successors after praiseworthy predecessors.
rows.anchor: ومن حق الخلفاء أن يسيروا بسيرة المستخلف من بعده ولا يخالفوه . ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjila ʿan al-amr means to leave a matter unfinished; its opposite is to complete it, and it can be made transitive by implication of 'precede'.
rows.anchor: يقال : عجل عن الأمر إذا تركه غير تام ، ونقيضه تم عليه وأعجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks whether Israel hastened past God's command instead of awaiting him and keeping his charge, supposing the appointment ended and he would not return.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أعجلتم عن أمر ربكم ، وهو انتظار موسى حافظين لعهده وما وصاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says the Samaritan told them Moses had died and would not return when he displayed the calf.
rows.anchor: وروي : أن السامري قال لهم حين أخرج لهم العجل وقال هذا إلاهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says they counted twenty days and nights as forty, then committed their deed.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنهم عدوا عشرين يوما بلياليها فجعلوها أربعين ، ثم أحدثوا ما أحدثوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses cast the tablets down in shock and distress on hearing of the calf, out of anger for God and zeal for His religion.
rows.anchor: وألقى الالواح } وطرحها لما لحقه من فرط الدهش وشدة الضجر عند استماعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was quick-tempered, while Aaron was gentler and therefore more loved by Israel.
rows.anchor: وكان في نفسه حديدا شديد الغضب ، وكان هارون ألين منه جانبا ولذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Torah had seven parts; after the tablets broke, six sevenths were lifted and one remained, containing all details and mercy.
rows.anchor: وروى : أن التوراة كانت سبعة أسباع ، فلما ألقى الألواح تكسرت فرفع منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking Aaron by the head means by his hair, dragging him by the forelock in the shock that clouded Moses' judgment as he suspected Aaron had failed to restrain the people.
rows.anchor: وأخذ برأس أخيه } أي بشعر رأسه { يجره إليه } بذؤابته وذلك لشدة ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn umm is read with fatḥa by analogy to khamsata ʿashara, with kasra by dropping the possessive yāʾ, also as ibn ummī with yāʾ and ibn imm with kasra on both letters.
rows.anchor: ابن أم } قرىء بالفتح تشبيها بخمسة عشر ، وبالكسر على طرح ياء الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Aaron was Moses' full brother; if so, Moses invoked their shared mother to awaken tenderness, stress their bond, and honor their believing mother and her suffering.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان أخاه لأبيه وأمه ، فإن صح فإنما أضافه إلى الأم ، إشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron says he did all he could through warning and admonition, but the people overpowered and weakened him and nearly killed him.
rows.anchor: إن القوم } يعني أنه لم يأل جهدا في كفهم بالوعظ والإنذار . وبما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is asked not to do what the enemies hoped for by humiliating or mistreating Aaron; a reading instead addresses the enemies, forbidding them to rejoice.
rows.anchor: فلا تشمت بى الاعداء } فلا تفعل بي ما هو أمنيتهم من الاستهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron asks not to be grouped with the wrongdoers in Moses' anger and punishment, or not to be regarded as one of them despite his innocence.
rows.anchor: ولا تجعلنى مع القوم الظالمين } ولا تجعلني في موجدتك علي وعقوبتك لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Aaron mentions the enemies' gloating, Moses asks forgiveness to reassure Aaron and show the onlookers that he is satisfied, preventing their glee.
rows.anchor: لما اعتذر إليه أخوه وذكر له شماتة الأعداء { قال رب اغفر لى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seeks forgiveness for his own excess toward Aaron and for Aaron in case he fell short in his stewardship.
rows.anchor: واستغفر لنفسه مما فرط منه إلى أخيه ، ولأخيه أن عسى فرط في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks that the brothers remain encompassed by God's mercy in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: وطلب أن لا يتفرقا عن رحمته ، ولا تزال منتظمة لهما في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened wrath is the command that they kill themselves; the humiliation is their expulsion, since exile is proverbial for abasement.
rows.anchor: الغضب ما أمروا به من قتل أنفسهم . والذلة : خروجهم من ديارهم لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view applies the wrath and humiliation to their descendants, the Qurayẓa and Naḍīr: killing and exile under God's anger, with humiliation through the poll tax.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو ما نال أبناءهم وهم بنو قريظة والنضير ، من غضب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forgers are liars against God; the Samaritan's claim that the calf was the god of Moses and Israel is the greatest fabrication.
rows.anchor: المفترين } المتكذبين على الله ، ولا فرية أعظم من قول السامري : هذا إلاهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'in the life of this world' may modify humiliation alone, placing God's wrath in the Hereafter and humiliation in this world.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق في الحياة الدنيا بالذلة وحدها ويراد : سيئا لهم غضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the wording to the verse saying abasement and poverty were imposed on them and they incurred God's anger.
rows.anchor: وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة وباؤوا بغضب من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil deeds encompass every kind of unbelief and sin; repentance is returning to God and seeking pardon, followed by sincere faith.
rows.anchor: والذين عملوا السيئات } من الكفر والمعاصي كلها { ثم تابوا } ثم رجعوا { من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After even grave sins, God conceals and erases them and grants Paradise; the rule applies to calf worshippers and everyone else.
rows.anchor: لغفور } لستور عليهم محاء لما كان منهم { رحيم } منعم عليهم بالجنة . وهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage first magnifies their offense and then God's mercy, showing that His pardon and generosity exceed even great sins.
rows.anchor: عظم جنايتهم أو لا ثم أردفها تعظيم رحمته ، ليعلم أن الذنوب وإن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance and turning back are necessary conditions; hope without them is empty and cold.
rows.anchor: ولكن لا بد من حفظ الشريطة : وهي وجوب التوبة والإنابة ، وما وراءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase personifies anger as urging Moses to speak and act; its eloquent force gives a reader with sound taste a jolt that the reading 'the anger subsided' lacks.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل ، كأن الغضب كان يغريه على ما فعل ويقول له : قل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading narrated from Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, 'when anger subsided from Moses,' lacks the emotional shock and awe of 'fell silent'.
rows.anchor: ولأنه من قبيل شعب البلاغة ، وإلا فما لقراءة معاوية بن قرة : ( ولما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is also read sakata or askata, meaning God or Aaron's apology silenced Moses' anger; the sense is that his anger went out.
rows.anchor: أي أسكته الله ، أو أخوه باعتذاره إليه وتنصله ، والمعنى : ولما طفىء غضبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tablets Moses took back are those he had thrown down.
rows.anchor: أخذ الالواح } التي ألقاها { وفى نسختها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuskhatihā means what was copied or written; nuskha is a feminine form with passive-object meaning, like khuṭba.
rows.anchor: وفى نسختها } وفيما نسخ منها ، أي كتب . والنسخة فعلة بمعنى مفعول كالخطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām before 'they fear' is placed before the verb because the object precedes it, which weakens the delayed verb; compare the phrasing in Joseph and 'for you I struck'.
rows.anchor: لربهم يرهبون } دخلت اللام ولتقدم المفعول ، لأن تأخر الفعل عن مفعوله يكسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 'Moses chose his people,' the preposition min is omitted and the verb made transitive, as in the cited poetic line.
rows.anchor: واختار موسى قومه } أي من قومه ، فحذف الجار أوصل الفعل ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Moses chose six from each of twelve tribes, making seventy-two; after two were to stay, they argued, and Caleb and Joshua remained after Moses promised equal reward.
rows.anchor: قيل : اختار من اثني عشر سبطا ، من كل سبط ستة حتى تتاموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says only sixty elders were available, so God told Moses to choose ten young men, who became elders by morning.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنه لم يصب إلا ستين شيخا ، فأوحى الله تعالى إليه أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says the men were twenty to forty, past ignorance and childhood; Moses ordered fasting and purification before taking them to Mount Sinai for God's appointment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا أبناء ما عدا العشرين ، ولم يتجاوزوا الأربعين ، قد ذهب عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says God ordered Moses to bring seventy Israelites; a cloud column covered the mountain, they entered and prostrated, heard God command Moses, then requested to see God; Moses asked to hear the refusal on their behalf, and the mountain shook as they fell unconscious.
rows.anchor: وكان أمره ربه أن يأتيه في سبعين من بني إسرائيل ، فلما دنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' wish that God had destroyed him and them earlier expresses regret at the consequence of their request to see God.
rows.anchor: وهذا تمن منه للإهلاك قبل أن يرى ما رأى من تبعة طلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Us' means Moses and the group: he had requested the vision to rebuke the foolish people, who asked for it in ignorance.
rows.anchor: يعني أتهلكنا جميعا ، يعني نفسه وإياهم ، لأنه إنما طلب الرؤية زجرا للسفهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial was God's speaking to Moses, which led the people to infer wrongly that they could see God and so fall into error.
rows.anchor: إن هى إلا فتنتك } أي محنتك وابتلاؤك حين كلمتني وسمعوا كلامك ، فاستدلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's causing some to stray and others to be guided is expressed by extension: the trial becomes the means by which the ignorant stray and the steadfast are guided.
rows.anchor: تضل بها من تشاء وتهدى من تشاء } تضل بالمحنة الجاهلين غير الثابتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attribution of their misguidance and guidance to God is figurative because His trial caused the two outcomes.
rows.anchor: وجعل ذلك إضلالا من الله وهدى منه ، لأن محنته لما كانت سببا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waliyyanā means our master, the one who manages our affairs.
rows.anchor: أنت ولينا } مولانا القائم بأمورنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uktub means establish, record, or allot for us a good in this world: well-being, a good life, and success in obedience; the good of the next life is Paradise.
rows.anchor: واكتب لنا } وأثبت لنا وأقسم { فى هاذه الدنيا حسنة } عافية وحياة طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadnā means we repented and returned to God; hāda ilāhi means to return and repent, and hūd is the plural of hāʾid, a penitent.
rows.anchor: هدنا إليك } تبنا إليك . وهاد إليه يهود إذا رجع وتاب . والهود : جمع

rows.speaker: أبو وجرة السعدي
rows.claim: Abū Wajra al-Saʿdī reads hidnā with kasra, from hāda meaning to move or incline; it can be active or passive, 'we moved ourselves toward You' or 'were moved toward You'.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو وجرة السعدي : ( هدنا إليك ) بكسر الهاء ، من هاده يهيده إما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative active/passive analyses are compared to variant vocalizations of ʿudtu, including the usage of visiting a sick person.
rows.anchor: كقولك : عدت يا مريض بكسر العين ، فعلت من العيادة . ويجوز : عدت بالإشمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ḍamma, hadnā may be the form of hāda yahīdu.
rows.anchor: ويجوز على هذه اللغة أن يكون { هدنا } بالضم فعلنا من هاده يهيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's punishment reaches whoever wisdom makes deserving of it, when pardon would cause harm.
rows.anchor: من حاله وصفته أني { أصيب به من أشاء } أي من وجب علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy is broad: Muslims and unbelievers, obedient and sinful, all live amid His blessings.
rows.anchor: فمن حالها وصفتها أنها واسعة تبلغ كل شيء ، ما من مسلم ولا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads man asāʾa, 'whoever does evil'.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( من أساء ) من الإساءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will reserve this mercy for end-time followers from Muhammad's community who believe in all God's signs and scriptures without rejecting any.
rows.anchor: فسأكتب هذه الرحمة كتبه خاصة منكم يا بني إسرائيل للذين يكونون في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger follows a scripture specifically revealed to him: the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: الذين يتبعون الرسول } الذي نوحي إليه كتابا مختصا به وهو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is the bearer of miracles.
rows.anchor: النبى } صاحب المعجزات { الذى يجدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites who follow him find his description written in the Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: الذى يجدونه } يجد نعته أولئك الذين يتبعونه من بني إسرائيل { مكتوبا عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permitted wholesome things include things formerly forbidden to them, such as animal fat, or things lawful under the revealed law: properly slaughtered meat and clean earnings.
rows.anchor: ويحل لهم الطيبات } ما حرم عليهم من الأشياء الطيبة ، كالشحوم وغيرها . أو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forbidden impurities include blood, carrion, pork, and offerings dedicated to other than God, or corrupt dealings such as usury and bribery.
rows.anchor: ويحرم عليهم الخبائث ما يستخبث من نحو الدم والميتة ولحم الخنزير ، وما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣr is a burden that restrains movement and represents the weight of Israel's difficult laws; the chains likewise represent onerous rules, including the cited examples.
rows.anchor: الإصر : الثقل الذي يأصر صاحبه ، أي يحبسه من الحراك لثقله وهو مثل

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says Israelites prayed wearing rough garments with their hands bound to their necks; some pierced a collarbone and chained themselves to a pillar to restrain themselves in worship.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء : كانت بنو إسرائيل إذا قامت تصلي لبسوا المسوح وغلوا أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣārahum is a plural reading of iṣr.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( آصارهم ) على الجمع { وعزروه } ومنعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzarahu means protected him from enemies; the shortened reading is also reported, and the root denotes prevention, as does taʿzīr, a discretionary punishment that restrains wrongdoing; ḥadd likewise means restraint.
rows.anchor: وعزروه } ومنعوه حتى لا يقوى عليه عدو . وقرىء بالتخفيف . وأصل العزر : المنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: و { النور } القرآن . فإن قلت : ما معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though revelation came with Gabriel, 'sent down with him' means that the Qur'an accompanied the Prophet's commissioning.
rows.anchor: قلت : معناه أنزل مع نبوته ، لأن استنباءه كان مصحوبا بالقرآن مشفوعا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase attaches to 'followed': they follow the Qur'an with their following of the Prophet and his practice, or follow the Qur'an as they follow the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يعلق باتبعوا . أي : واتبعوا القرآن المنزل مع اتباع النبي والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to Moses' prayer for himself and Israel implicitly rebukes Israel for demanding to see God and rejecting God's great signs shown through Moses.
rows.anchor: لما دعا لنفسه ولبني إسرائيل ، أجيب بما هو منطو على توبيخ بني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of those who believe God's signs points toward faithful converts such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, encouraging the People of the Book to sincere faith and good works and to join their descendants under God's all-encompassing mercy.
rows.anchor: وعرض بذلك في قوله : { والذين هم بئاياتنا يؤمنون } وأريد أن يكون استماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's verse urges the sinner to repent and prostrate, illustrating hadnā as turning back to God.
rows.anchor: يا راكب الذنب هدهد … واسجد كأنك هدهد
